question: How do uterine contractions help during a medical abortion?

options.A: They push the gestational sac down and out through the dilated cervix
options.B: They raise blood pressure to flush out toxins
options.C: They permanently numb pelvic nerves so there is zero pain
options.D: They seal off the uterine lining to stop hormones

explanation: Once the cervix is soft, those rhythmic uterine contractions create the gentle pressure needed to clear the pregnancy tissue safely.

question: What is the main job of the rod cells in your retina?

options.A: Processing sharp color details in bright light
options.B: Adjusting focus for near objects
options.C: Controlling the size of the pupil
options.D: Handling night and side vision

explanation: You got it! Rods are your night-vision heroes. They are super sensitive to dim light, helping you see in the dark and catch movement out of the corner of your eye.

question: What is the number one direct cause of maternal death all over the world?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Severe dehydration
options.C: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Severe bleeding after childbirth (PPH) is the leading global killer of new mothers. As a nurse, knowing how to spot and manage PPH can literally save a life!

question: When is the best time to encourage a patient to attempt bowel evacuation during a training program?

options.A: Right after waking up in the middle of the night
options.B: Whenever abdominal pain starts
options.C: Immediately before going to sleep
options.D: Shortly after eating a meal

explanation: Eating triggers the natural gastrocolic reflex, making the bowels more active and responsive to scheduled evacuation attempts. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h6)

question: What do we mean by 'microbial load' in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: The total number of microorganisms on a contaminated object
options.B: The specific type of chemical disinfectant used on instruments
options.C: The weight of dry garbage collected in a hospital ward
options.D: The maximum capacity limit of an incinerator furnace

explanation: You've got this! Microbial load simply refers to the total count of living germs on a surface or waste item. The higher the load, the more dangerous that item is if someone handles it carelessly.

question: How does individualizing a medication schedule help a patient?

options.A: It allows the nurse to finish the shift much earlier
options.B: It lowers the financial cost of buying the medications from the pharmacy
options.C: It fits the drug timing into their normal daily routine to prevent missed doses
options.D: It stops the drug from causing any side effects in the body

explanation: When drugs match a person's daily habits, they are much easier to remember and take consistently. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is the key difference between general negligence and professional malpractice?

options.A: Negligence requires a written contract, whereas malpractice does not
options.B: Negligence only happens in surgical theatres, while malpractice happens in outpatient clinics
options.C: Malpractice carries a prison sentence, whereas negligence is always ignored by the courts
options.D: Malpractice involves professional standards of care by a licensed specialist, while negligence is general careless behavior

explanation: Malpractice is a specific type of professional negligence committed by a person holding a specialized license. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h7)

question: Which part of the brainstem contains the main control hubs for heart rate and breathing rhythms?

options.A: Cerebellum
options.B: Medulla oblongata
options.C: Midbrain
options.D: Cerebral cortex

explanation: The medulla oblongata is like the engine room of your brain, keeping your heart beating and your lungs breathing smoothly.

question: What is the main job of the ovaries in the female body?

options.A: Storing urine before it reaches the bladder
options.B: Producing eggs and female hormones
options.C: Filtering waste from the lower abdomen
options.D: Producing red blood cells during pregnancy

explanation: You got this! The ovaries are our female reproductive glands that make ova (eggs) and important hormones like estrogen and progesterone.

question: A family member asks how to help a relative overcome a bad driving phobia. What is the best advice to give?

options.A: Do all the driving for them so they never feel anxious again
options.B: Insist they drive on busy highways immediately to get over it
options.C: Hide all car keys so they forget about driving completely
options.D: Encourage small steps of progress and avoid enabling total avoidance

explanation: Doing everything for them (enabling) makes the phobia stronger. Families should cheer on small, brave steps forward instead!

question: What makes an intragroup conflict unique among nurses on the same ward?

options.A: It happens among members of the exact same team.
options.B: It arises strictly from a lack of hospital medical equipment.
options.C: It only occurs between nurses and hospital administrators.
options.D: It involves a nurse arguing with a patient's family member.

explanation: Intragroup conflict happens right within a single, close-knit team—like coworkers on your own shift disagreeing on how to run things.

question: Why should nurse educators review student feedback regarding their teaching methods?

options.A: To find out which students said negative things and lower their clinical scores
options.B: To identify their own instructional weaknesses and improve future lessons
options.C: To prove to the hospital administration that no changes are ever needed
options.D: To comply with local tax laws for higher education institutions

explanation: Good teachers love feedback! It helps them see what worked for the students and how they can explain things better next time.

question: Why is knowing the route of transmission important for a nurse?

options.A: It eliminates the need for hand hygiene in clean wards
options.B: It predicts the exact day the patient will be discharged
options.C: It determines which antibiotic the doctor will prescribe first
options.D: It helps choose the correct isolation and barrier precautions

explanation: When nurses know how a germ travels, they can block that path using masks, gloves, or specific room placements. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC)?

options.A: Male latex condom
options.B: Spermicidal foam
options.C: Intrauterine device
options.D: Oral contraceptive pill

explanation: An Intrauterine Device (IUD) is placed in the womb and provides protection for years, but can be removed anytime you want.

question: A patient with a bacterial infection wants to stop taking antibiotics after two days because they feel fine. What should you tell them?

options.A: They must double the remaining dose on the third day instead
options.B: They should save the remaining pills for a headache next week
options.C: Stopping early can cause the infection to return stronger and more resistant
options.D: It is completely safe to stop once fever symptoms disappear

explanation: You got it! Always encourage patients to finish the full dose so the infection doesn't bounce back stronger.

question: Which of these actions does NOT support safe patient care by a nurse leader?

options.A: Maintaining adequate staffing levels for patient acuity
options.B: Ensuring evidence-based clinical guidelines are followed
options.C: Punishing staff publicly for reporting near-misses
options.D: Promoting open communication and incident reporting

explanation: Spot on! Publicly punishing staff for speaking up only creates fear, making people hide their mistakes and putting patients at greater risk.

question: Why do nurses need to look beyond the hospital walls when caring for patients?

options.A: Clinical treatments alone are completely useless without government approval
options.B: Patients expect nurses to solve their personal family conflicts
options.C: Hospital regulations require documentation of a patient's financial status
options.D: External economic, social, and cultural forces deeply shape a person's health outcomes

explanation: You've got this! Remember that health doesn't start and stop at the hospital doors. A patient's daily life, money, and community heavily influence their healing. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why is it a mistake for a nurse manager to panic over every single normal, everyday variation?

options.A: It causes the hospital to lose its government license.
options.B: It creates unnecessary panic and wastes effort trying to fix a process that is working normally.
options.C: It forces staff to stop checking vital signs.
options.D: It instantly stops all new patient admissions to the ward.

explanation: Every day won't look identical. Overreacting to normal day-to-day fluctuations just stresses out the team for no reason!

question: Which disease is classically transmitted via the airborne route?

options.A: Scabies
options.B: Hepatitis B
options.C: Malaria
options.D: Tuberculosis

explanation: Tuberculosis spreads through tiny airborne droplets released when an infected person coughs or speaks. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h4)

question: What is the main job of synovial fluid inside a freely moving joint?

options.A: To lubricate the joint and nourish the cartilage
options.B: To produce new red blood cells for the joint space
options.C: To anchor skeletal muscles directly to the bone ends
options.D: To generate electrical impulses for joint movement

explanation: Synovial fluid acts like oil in a car engine. It keeps movements smooth and feeds the cartilage since blood vessels don't reach right into it.

question: What happens during codominance?

options.A: Mutations destroy both alleles before birth
options.B: The physical traits from both parents blend together completely
options.C: Both alleles are expressed equally and independently
options.D: One dominant allele completely hides the recessive allele

explanation: In codominance, neither allele masks the other; both are fully visible in the organism, such as in AB blood groups. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the main goal of genetic counseling for couples in communities with high sickle cell rates?

options.A: To test newborns for immediate signs of acute chest syndrome
options.B: To provide accurate information on inheritance risks for family planning
options.C: To administer prophylactic antibiotics to prevent bacterial infections
options.D: To prescribe daily doses of folic acid for blood cell production

explanation: Counseling empowers couples with clear facts about their genotypes so they can make informed, confident family planning choices.

question: Which bioethical principle is about sharing scarce resources fairly during a disaster?

options.A: Veracity
options.B: Justice
options.C: Paternalism
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Well done! Justice means making sure medical care and resources are distributed fairly without unfair bias during a crisis.

question: How many core elements make up the standard post-abortion care framework?

options.A: Ten
options.B: Three
options.C: Seven
options.D: Five

explanation: You got it! The standard PAC framework is built on five key elements that guide clinical care and community support.

question: During a home visit, the nurse sees loose scatter rugs on the floor. What is the best advice?

options.A: Recommend removing all loose rugs to prevent accidental slips and falls
options.B: Tape the edges of the rugs down securely with masking tape
options.C: Leave the rugs in place because they provide essential cushion
options.D: Instruct the patient to walk faster when crossing the rugs

explanation: You nailed it! Loose rugs are a major tripping hazard and should be cleared away for safety.

question: When should a nurse refer a postpartum mother to a specialized family planning clinic?

options.A: When a new mother refuses to hold her baby after a normal delivery
options.B: When routine postpartum lochia transitions from red to yellow-white
options.C: When the infant develops mild neonatal jaundice in the first week
options.D: When a client has a complex medical history requiring expert evaluation

explanation: Mums with underlying health conditions like severe high blood pressure need expert guidance to pick the safest contraceptive method.

question: What is the main focus of embryology?

options.A: The analysis of genetic mutations during adult life
options.B: The microscopic examination of human bone tissue
options.C: The study of prenatal development from fertilization to birth
options.D: The physical changes that occur during normal aging

explanation: Embryology simply looks at how a new baby grows and develops inside the womb, right from the very first cell union up until birth. You've got this!

question: What is a major benefit of using physiological measures like a blood pressure machine in research?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any human researchers
options.B: They cost nothing to purchase and maintain
options.C: They take the place of nursing clinical judgment
options.D: They provide objective data that cannot be falsified by memory

explanation: Physiological tools measure physical states directly, providing reliable, objective data without relying on patient memory. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h5)

question: Why do nurses need to understand health care costs?

options.A: To diagnose complex financial diseases in the community
options.B: To calculate daily profits for the hospital pharmacy
options.C: To help patients navigate financial strain and advocate for them
options.D: To replace hospital accountants during budget reviews

explanation: You will often see how money worries affect your patients. Knowing about healthcare costs helps you support and speak up for them when they face tough financial choices.

question: Why did military nursing groups become so important during the Crusades?

options.A: To translate ancient Greek philosophy texts
options.B: To provide organized shelter and treat wounded soldiers
options.C: To manufacture advanced gunpowder and tactical weapons
options.D: To govern newly conquered political territories

explanation: During the Crusades, special nursing groups were needed to set up safe resting places and care for fighters and travelers who got hurt.

question: Why is it usually unfair and unhelpful to immediately blame an individual nurse when a clinical mistake happens?

options.A: It forces the patient to leave the healthcare facility prematurely
options.B: It automatically increases the financial budget of the hospital ward
options.C: It violates international nursing licensing laws instantly
options.D: It ignores underlying system and psychological factors that caused the mistake

explanation: Most mistakes happen because of faulty systems or rushed environments, not because a nurse doesn't care. Fixing the system stops the error from happening again!

question: A patient is having a sudden panic attack on the ward. What is the best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop worrying about nothing
options.B: Guiding the patient through slow, controlled breathing exercises
options.C: Administering a high-dose herbal supplement immediately
options.D: Leaving the patient alone in a quiet room to sleep

explanation: Deep, slow breathing triggers the body's calming system, helping to physically slow down anxiety and panic right away.

question: Why is it important to use a mix of different data collection tools during a community diagnosis?

options.A: It is a legal requirement set by international pharmaceutical companies
options.B: It reduces the amount of time needed to write the final report
options.C: It helps verify findings and provides a more complete picture of health needs
options.D: It ensures that every single resident is interviewed personally

explanation: Combining surveys, interviews, and observations allows nurses to cross-verify data and understand both numbers and human experiences. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h7)

question: Which of these is considered a direct cost of a physical disability?

options.A: Losing daily wages while resting
options.B: Missing a promotion due to bias
options.C: Reduced workplace productivity
options.D: Buying a wheelchair and mobility braces

explanation: Direct costs are the actual out-of-pocket prices you pay for items specifically needed because of the impairment, like assistive devices and drugs.

question: Early in your research journey, how does having a theoretical framework help you?

options.A: Clear research questions
options.B: The hospital budget
options.C: The nursing shift schedule
options.D: Patient discharge summaries

explanation: Well done! A good framework shines a light on what you need to study, making it much easier to write sharp and focused research questions.

question: What is a major reason why quacks and illegal clinics are still able to operate in some communities?

options.A: Inadequate funding and a shortage of regulatory inspectors
options.B: Strict enforcement of immediate prison sentences by local police
options.C: Excessive availability of advanced medical diagnostic machines
options.D: Mandatory participation in international nursing conferences

explanation: When regulatory bodies don't have enough money or enough inspectors to cover every corner, illegal clinics unfortunately manage to slip through the cracks.

question: Who typically conducts follow-up visits or phone checks during a patient's trial leave?

options.A: Local law enforcement officers on routine patrol
options.B: Hospital security guards and accountants
options.C: Community psychiatric nurses or outpatient clinic staff
options.D: Pharmacy delivery workers with no medical training

explanation: Community psychiatric nurses and clinic staff are your go-to pros for keeping in touch and offering guidance during trial leave.

question: A family brings their relative to a psychiatric clinic after months of visiting prayer houses for sudden aggressive behavior. What should the nurse understand about this situation?

options.A: The family clearly does not care about the patient's well-being at all
options.B: Traditional and religious methods always cure mental disorders completely
options.C: Cultural and spiritual beliefs heavily influence care-seeking pathways in Nigeria
options.D: The psychiatric nurse should scold the family for wasting precious time

explanation: Understanding that families often consult spiritual or traditional sources first helps nurses provide non-judgmental education and build trust. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is regular monitoring and evaluation essential for public health campaigns against harmful practices?

options.A: To collect financial fines from communities that fail to comply
options.B: To replace local nurses with international researchers
options.C: To create strict academic exams for regional healthcare workers
options.D: To measure progress, track prevalence, and adjust ineffective strategies

explanation: Tracking data shows whether programs are actually reducing harmful practices or if new approaches are needed. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h8)

question: What is an example of closed-loop communication during a resuscitation?

options.A: Calling out for extra help over the hospital public address system
options.B: Repeating an order back to the leader to confirm it was heard and understood
options.C: Nodding your head silently when the doctor walks into the room
options.D: Writing down all medications on a paper chart after the code ends

explanation: Closed-loop communication prevents dangerous mistakes by ensuring every order is clearly acknowledged and verified. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h8)

question: Which characteristic of an effective nursing plan allows it to adapt to sudden patient admissions?

options.A: Secrecy
options.B: Rigidity
options.C: Complexity
options.D: Flexibility

explanation: Healthcare changes constantly, so a plan must be flexible enough to bend when emergencies happen. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h2)

question: How can a community health nurse best address local suspicion regarding health surveys?

options.A: Ignore the suspicious residents and only interview hospital staff
options.B: Collect data secretly at night without telling community members
options.C: Involve respected local leaders and explain the purpose clearly
options.D: Threaten residents with fines if they refuse to answer questions

explanation: Partnering with trusted community figures helps dispel myths and reassures residents that the health activities are safe and beneficial. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h8)

question: Which group of people usually suffers the most from long-term parasitic infections?

options.A: Elderly men
options.B: Adolescent athletes
options.C: Office workers
options.D: Young children

explanation: Young children are especially vulnerable to parasites. These little bugs can steal their nutrients and slow down their growth, which is why child health education is so vital!

question: What does the popular '60/60 rule' recommend when using earphones or headphones?

options.A: Listening at no more than sixty percent volume for sixty minutes daily
options.B: Taking a sixty-minute break after every sixty steps taken
options.C: Keeping the device sixty inches away from the ears at all times
options.D: Using headphones for no more than sixty hours a week

explanation: The 60/60 rule is an easy trick to protect your ears from loud music damage. Try keeping your volume at 60% or lower for no more than 60 minutes a day!

question: What is the main purpose of the watery fluid secreted in the small intestine?

options.A: To kill bacteria before they can reach the large intestine
options.B: To provide a liquid medium that aids nutrient absorption
options.C: To act as a strong acid that breaks down complex proteins
options.D: To emulsify dietary fats into tiny water-soluble droplets

explanation: Fluid keeps everything dissolved nicely so the intestinal walls can easily absorb the nutrients your body needs.

question: Why can forcing large meals cause problems for a patient with an advanced illness?

options.A: It causes physical distress like nausea and cramping
options.B: It instantly cures the loss of appetite
options.C: It interferes with daily physical therapy
options.D: It speeds up the metabolism too quickly

explanation: Spot on! When the body is weak, its digestive system slows down. Heavy meals just lead to discomfort like belly pain and nausea, rather than good nutrition.

question: How can tele-nursing work best in rural areas with limited resources?

options.A: By requiring patients to buy expensive personal computers before getting help
options.B: By waiting until every village has advanced fibre-optic internet cables installed
options.C: By stopping all physical hospital care and replacing it with mobile apps
options.D: By utilizing simple, accessible tools like basic SMS and solar-powered communication points

explanation: You got it! Success in resource-limited settings depends on using affordable, everyday technology that fits local realities rather than waiting for fancy equipment.

question: What shape does a perfectly balanced, symmetrical data distribution make?

options.A: A flat horizontal line
options.B: A bell-shaped curve
options.C: An upward sloping diagonal
options.D: A sharp V-shape

explanation: Nice one! A normal distribution makes a lovely bell shape where the mean, median, and mode all sit right in the center together.

question: Why might you prefer the interquartile range over the simple range when looking at how long patients stay in the hospital?

options.A: It is much faster to calculate by hand without a calculator
options.B: It ignores extreme outliers like a few patients staying for months
options.C: It directly measures the exact average of the data set
options.D: It includes every single data point in the final calculation

explanation: Sometimes a couple of patients stay for months and throw off the simple range. The interquartile range focuses on the middle 50% so you get a clearer picture of a normal stay.

question: When should a nurse ideally start rehab care for a hospitalized patient?

options.A: As soon as the patient is medically stable
options.B: After the patient is completely discharged home
options.C: When the family requests assistance with daily tasks
options.D: Only when all physical therapy orders are finished

explanation: Great thinking! Starting early stops stiff joints and weak muscles before they even start.

question: Which popular Nigerian vegetable is well-known as a fantastic plant source of iron?

options.A: Fluted pumpkin leaves (Ugu)
options.B: Jute mallow (Ewedu)
options.C: Waterleaf
options.D: African garden egg

question: What is an important nursing duty when a pregnant patient is given an antiemetic drug?

options.A: Encourage the patient to stop taking all oral fluids
options.B: Advise the patient to double the dose if nausea returns
options.C: Check fetal heart tones every fifteen minutes around the clock
options.D: Monitor the patient for common side effects like drowsiness

explanation: Many antiemetics make patients sleepy. Keeping an eye on safety and advising them about drowsiness is a key nursing role.

question: What is a major difference between thoracic spinal nerves and the nerves in the neck or lower back?

options.A: Thoracic nerves only carry sensory information
options.B: Thoracic nerves do not connect to the spinal cord
options.C: Thoracic nerves do not form complex nerve plexuses
options.D: Thoracic nerves lack ventral roots

explanation: While other regions braid together into big webs (plexuses), thoracic nerves stay independent as clean, separate intercostal nerves between the ribs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h6)

question: What stops large blood proteins and red blood cells from entering the filtrate in a healthy kidney?

options.A: Enzymes lining the proximal tubule
options.B: High pressure inside the collecting duct
options.C: The tight filtration barrier of the glomerulus
options.D: Active transport pumps in the loop of Henle

explanation: The membrane of the glomerulus features specialized pores and slits that prevent large cells and proteins from leaving the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h2)

question: A doctor dismisses your drug dose warning with sarcasm. What should you do next as an assertive nurse?

options.A: Reiterate the safety data calmly and firmly
options.B: Apologize for wasting the doctor's time
options.C: Complain loudly to the patients in the ward
options.D: Throw the medication chart on the desk

explanation: Standing your ground with calm facts ensures patient safety remains the top priority despite resistance. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h7)

question: What standard manual do mental health professionals use to classify mental disorders?

options.A: Nursing Interventions Classification Handbook
options.B: International Directory of Psychiatric Medications
options.C: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders
options.D: Standard Medical Treatment Guidelines for Africa

explanation: You'll hear this called the DSM! It's the standard guidebook clinicians use around the world to properly diagnose and categorize mental health conditions.

question: What is the main purpose of pre-positioned warehouses set up around the world by disaster agencies?

options.A: To collect financial taxes from incoming humanitarian workers
options.B: To store emergency supplies strategically around the globe for rapid dispatch
options.C: To manufacture local pharmaceutical drugs during an epidemic
options.D: To serve as permanent housing units for refugees fleeing conflict

explanation: You got it! Keeping emergency gear stocked near disaster-prone areas means supplies can reach the field much faster.

question: During a sudden emergency on the ward, the charge nurse gives quick, direct orders without debating. What leadership style is this?

options.A: Democratic
options.B: Laissez-Faire
options.C: Autocratic
options.D: Transformational

explanation: In an emergency, there's no time for a committee meeting! An autocratic style gives fast, clear direction when every second counts.

question: When should public health nurses begin control measures during a suspected disease outbreak?

options.A: Only when international health agencies give direct written permission
options.B: As soon as strong clinical evidence suggests an outbreak, without waiting for every lab result
options.C: Only after writing a final research paper for an academic journal
options.D: After all affected patients have been completely discharged from the hospital

explanation: Exactly! In public health, speed saves lives. Waiting for every single lab result can cause preventable harm. Great clinical instinct!

question: A nurse notices two coworkers refusing to speak to each other, which is now delaying patient treatments. What is happening here?

options.A: Unresolved staff conflict is spilling over into patient care quality.
options.B: Intrapersonal conflict is helping the nurses focus on their duties.
options.C: The unit is experiencing a normal latent phase of conflict.
options.D: The nurses are successfully using healthy debate to solve a problem.

explanation: Personal grudges among staff should never hurt patient care. When bad blood slows down clinical tasks, team conflict has unfortunately crossed the line into harming patients.

question: Which of the following practices is NOT permitted when handling electronic patient information?

options.A: Sending identifiable patient records through unsecured personal messaging apps
options.B: Locking computer screens when walking away from a hospital workstation
options.C: Verifying the recipient's identity before sending clinical notes
options.D: Using end-to-end encrypted software for telehealth discussions

explanation: Unsecured personal apps lack proper encryption and violate patient privacy laws, making them unsafe for sharing identifiable health data. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h6)

question: A client presents with a sudden worsening cough and shortness of breath. Which interview question is most important to ask first?

options.A: How many family members have asthma?
options.B: What kind of work did you do thirty years ago?
options.C: Are you allergic to any specific types of food?
options.D: When did these breathing symptoms actually start?

explanation: Determining the onset and timeline of acute symptoms is the immediate priority during a symptom analysis for a sudden respiratory change. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of a formative evaluation during your nursing training?

options.A: To determine if a nurse is ready to receive a professional license.
options.B: To assign a final grade at the very end of a nursing program.
options.C: To compare a student's score against national averages.
options.D: To provide ongoing feedback and guide student improvement during learning.

explanation: Formative evaluations are like friendly practice checkpoints—they happen along the way to help you catch mistakes and grow before the final exams!

question: Why does primary health care place heavy emphasis on nutrition and safe water alongside medical treatment?

options.A: Nurses are trained as civil engineers rather than clinicians
options.B: Preventing disease through basic sanitation stops sickness before it starts
options.C: Doctors refuse to treat patients who do not drink boiled water
options.D: Water and food are more profitable than pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Clean water and good nutrition address the root environmental causes of infection, reducing the burden on clinics. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why is taking ART medications every single day so important for patients?

options.A: Missing a single dose causes immediate death from opportunistic infections.
options.B: Inconsistent taking of drugs can cause the virus to mutate and develop resistance to treatment.
options.C: Taking pills at irregular times makes the medication taste much worse.
options.D: Strict adherence is only necessary during the first month of therapy.

explanation: Consistency is key! If a patient skips doses, drug levels drop in the blood, giving the crafty virus a chance to change its form and beat the medicine.

question: What is a major ethical worry when using tele-nursing communication?

options.A: Preventing patients from buying medications at local pharmacies
options.B: Ensuring that nurses get paid a higher salary than physicians
options.C: Maintaining patient privacy and data confidentiality over digital networks
options.D: Eliminating the need to write nursing notes in patient files

explanation: Well reasoned! Sending health info over phones or the internet can expose it to unauthorized people, making data privacy a huge ethical duty for nurses.

question: A patient with a head injury has their brain pressure (ICP) spike every time care is given. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Space out nursing care activities and avoid sudden neck flexion
options.B: Stop all neurological assessments for the remainder of the shift
options.C: Encourage family members to talk loudly to stimulate the patient
options.D: Lower the head of the bed completely flat to rest the patient

explanation: Doing everything at once can overwhelm a sensitive brain. Spacing out tasks and keeping the neck straight helps keep pressure stable.

question: Why do community health nurses look at accidents as things we can prevent rather than just 'bad luck'?

options.A: Because bad luck cannot be studied scientifically
options.B: Because most accidents follow preventable patterns
options.C: Because hospitals profit directly from treating injuries
options.D: Because government policies cause all accidents

explanation: Spotting accidents as preventable events helps us design safety steps that keep our communities safe and injury-free!

question: A nurse notices a patient's blood pressure dropping rapidly and calls the doctor using SBAR. What information should be stated in the Recommendation part?

options.A: What action or intervention is needed right now
options.B: A summary of yesterday's nursing shift notes
options.C: The patient's full medical history from childhood
options.D: The exact cost of the patient's hospital room

explanation: Correct! The 'Recommendation' is where you clearly state what you need done right now to help stabilize your patient.

question: Why are deworming tablets often given alongside school feeding programs?

options.A: Intestinal worms cause nutrient loss and anemia in children
options.B: Deworming tablets sweeten the drinking water supply

options.D: Worms prevent children from catching common cold viruses

question: What is the most common nutritional problem facing adolescent girls in Nigeria today?

options.B: Beriberi from polished rice

question: What happens if you accidentally use cold water to flush a patient's ear?

options.B: The eardrum will automatically seal itself tighter

question: Which of these is a misuse of a theoretical framework in a research project?

question: How should community mental health nurses best approach traditional healers?

options.A: Through respectful dialogue and collaborative education

options.D: By adopting all of their religious rituals into the hospital

question: Which of these sits at the very top of the healthcare policy framework?

options.A: Ward shift handover notes

options.D: Individual departmental protocols

question: How can Nigerian nurses break through barriers that keep them out of health planning rooms?

options.A: By ignoring hospital management and making independent laws

question: Why should we make sure marginalized or vulnerable groups have a voice in community health committees?

question: What is the main job of a research hypothesis?

options.A: To summarize the demographic data

options.A: Dry heat sterilization in an oven
options.B: Simple rinse under cold tap water

question: During a massive flood, what is the primary role of security agencies like the police?

options.A: Crowd control, maintenance of law and order, and safe corridors

options.C: Clinical triage and emergency surgical interventions at the bedside

options.A: Papule

question: What does 'psychological safety' mean for a clinical healthcare team?

options.A: Patients never experience any physical complications or infections

question: What is a main duty of an occupational health nurse working as a case manager?

options.A: Conducting annual financial audits for human resources
